title: Operate and Secure Events
readerIntent: Monitor delivery, control backlogs, recover failures, and qualify providers.
priorKnowledge: Know event types, destinations, guarantees, retry, and recovery ownership.
owner: Event owners, NEMS operators, and configured transport provider
summary: Operations must expose safe delivery outcomes, lag, retries, duplicates, poison messages, provider health, and manual recovery without leaking event payloads.

sections.heading: Monitor
items: Publish, consume, success, failure, retry, replay, and duplicate rates.
End-to-end delivery latency, backlog, oldest age, and consumer lag.
Provider connection, acknowledgement, rejection, throttle, and reconnect state.
Failed definitions, event logs, manual recovery, and cleanup outcomes.

sections.heading: Secure
items: Authorize publish and consume by governed event and destination contracts.
Encrypt transport and use least-privilege identities.
Validate tenant, source, target, version, size, and payload schema.
Redact payloads, credentials, personal data, and internal provider errors.

sections.heading: Recover and qualify
items: Pause or isolate poison messages without blocking unrelated partitions.
Replay only with authorization, idempotency, audit, and bounded scope.
Test broker loss, consumer crash, redelivery, duplicate, out-of-order delivery, network partition, backlog recovery, and shutdown.
Prove claimed guarantees with the live provider and production-like topology.

sections.heading: Backpressure and capacity
items: Bound publisher rate, payload size, consumer concurrency, prefetch, retry, and backlog.
Scale consumers by partition and idempotency constraints.
Protect databases and remote services from backlog replay bursts.
Alert on oldest-message age and recovery-time risk.
Load and soak test representative payloads and failure rates.

sections.heading: Incident workflow
paragraphs: For growing backlog, preserve evidence, identify provider, consumer, dependency, or poison-message cause, then pause or isolate affected partitions if needed. Restore bounded consumption and observe authoritative side effects.
For suspected cross-tenant delivery, stop the affected path, preserve audit evidence, assess exposure, correct routing and authorization, and reconcile all impacted events.

sections.heading: Replay governance
items: Authorized requester and approved reason.
Bounded event types, tenants, identities, and time range.
Consumer idempotency and side-effect assessment.
Rate limits and dependency capacity.
Dry-run or preview where supported.
Audit, outcome reconciliation, and rollback or compensation.

sections.heading: Production readiness
items: Qualified provider versions, TLS, credentials, destinations, and topology.
Delivery, acknowledgement, ordering, redelivery, and retention evidence.
Load, outage, partition, failover, restart, replay, and upgrade tests.
Dashboards, alerts, runbooks, dead-letter or failed-state ownership.
Backup or persisted-state recovery and scheduled cleanup.
